links.outcome: Local accuracy of IED detection software versus clinical reference standard at default setting
links.effect: Sensitivity 81.1% (95% CI 77.6-84.6), specificity 59.9%, PPV 19.9%, NPV 96.3%; high NPV but low PPV with potential over-calling of IEDs.
links.quote: At P15's default sensitivity setting, sensitivity for IED detection was 81.1% (95% CI:77.6-84.6), specificity 59.9% (95% CI: 55.5-64.2), positive predictive value 19.9% (95% CI:16.3-23.5) and negative predictive value 96.3% (95% CI:94.6-98.0).

links.outcome: Predictive values at local prevalence of IEDs in routine EEGs
links.effect: With 53 of 484 records IED-positive, PPV was 19.9% and NPV 96.3%, showing utility differs from pre-selected IED-rich datasets.
links.quote: Previous evaluations of machine learning models have reported non-inferiority compared to human experts, but these studies predominantly use small datasets of pre-selected, 'IED rich' records, which are not representative of clinical practice.

screen.reason: Evaluates commercial automated EEG spike detection software (P15) retrospectively against clinical reports in a routine clinical cohort, focusing on diagnostic accuracy without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
